s1.syndrome_frame: Acute liver failure with hemodynamic shock and cholestasis following liver transplantation
salient_findings: Intra-abdominal bleeding from a choledochal artery branch
key_facts: 52-year-old man with HCV-associated end-stage cirrhosis
Underwent liver transplantation
Required relaparotomy due to intra-abdominal bleeding
Initial liver function improved
Cholestasis observed on day 4
Persistent abdominal pain reported on day 6
Fulminant liver failure and hemodynamic shock developed by day 7
Single fever peak of 38.4°C on day 8
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, GGT, ALP) on day 6
Total bilirubin level of 119 μmol/L on day 6
Positive blood culture on day 7
Positive liver graft, colon, and small bowel biopsy samples on day 9

shortlist.label: Sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive blood culture and clinical signs of hemodynamic shock

shortlist.label: Ischemia-reperfusion injury
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated liver enzymes and fulminant liver failure after liver transplantation

shortlist.label: Primary graft dysfunction
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse liver necrosis and initial liver function improvement followed by rapid decline

shortlist.label: Bacteremia
shortlist.why_kept: Positive blood culture and positive liver graft, colon, and small bowel biopsy samples

shortlist.label: Rejection of liver transplant
shortlist.why_kept: Fulminant liver failure and hemodynamic shock despite initial improvement after transplantation

raw.rationale: The patient developed fulminant liver failure, hemodynamic shock, and had positive blood cultures and biopsy samples, indicating a severe infection.

rejected.label: Ischemia-reperfusion injury
rejected.why: While possible, the timeline and presence of positive cultures suggest an infectious cause rather than just ischemia-reperfusion injury

rejected.label: Primary graft dysfunction
rejected.why: Primary graft dysfunction typically occurs immediately after transplantation, but the patient's initial liver function improved before declining

rejected.label: Bacteremia
rejected.why: Bacteremia is a component of the patient's condition but does not fully explain the fulminant liver failure and other symptoms

rejected.label: Rejection of liver transplant
rejected.why: Rejection would not typically cause such rapid deterioration and does not account for the positive cultures and biopsy results
